name: Watching
summary: Follow goals you don’t own: they show on your Home and under Watching in Goals.

rebuild.builds: Watching, as a feature a workspace can switch off. Anyone can watch a goal, a goal and everything feeding it, or every goal at a level; the goals a person's watches cover are on their Home under “Goals you watch” (what needs attention first) and under the Watching tab of Goals, a goal's page has Watch (or Watching) for anyone but its owner, and an AI tool lists, adds and stops watches. Off, there is no Watching tab, no “Goals you watch”, no Watch button and no watching tool; /watching says it is switched off and who can switch it on; someone who owns no goal is led to every goal that needs attention. Every watch is kept, and switching it back on restores each person's. An admin switches it off on Workspace, Features, after a read-back that counts what stays.
entry: The core rules (stage 1) work out each goal's status, flags and attention; Watching reads them and adds nothing to them.
The core keeps a workspace's switched-off modules (Workspace.modulesOff) and refuses a switched-off module's actions and AI tools (stage 2).
exit: Switched off, /watching shows Page not found with “Watching is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, Features.”, and list_watching, watch and unwatch answer “Watching is switched off in {workspace}, so {tool} can’t be used there. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, under Features.” (check N22).

Switched off, Goals has no Watching tab (a remembered Watching tab opens Mine, or All for someone who owns no goal), Home has no “Goals you watch”, a goal's page has no Watch or Watching and no “Watched by”, and the watch action refuses with “Watching is off in {workspace}.” (journey U156).
Switched off, someone who owns no goal is led to “{n} goals need attention · See them” (every goal that needs attention), not to the goals they watch.

Switching off first reads back what stays, from the rule watchingOffReadBack: how many people's watches are kept, and how many of them own no goal and see Home through what they watch; with no watch at all it acts at once.
Back on, every person watches what they did (journey U156).
gaps: Watching is a switch, not yet a folder of its own (SW6 moves it): its screens (src/screens/Watching.tsx; Home's “Goals you watch” in src/screens/Home.tsx; the Watch button and its sheet in src/screens/GoalScreen.tsx; the Watching tab of src/screens/GoalsScreen.tsx), its rules (src/domain/watch.ts, src/domain/review.ts watchedGoals, src/domain/home.ts groupWatched, src/domain/goalsPage.ts scopesFor) and its actions (watch and unwatch in src/domain/actions.ts) are still the core's, and so is its table (okr_watches, migration 0006). The watch actions refuse while it is off in src/app/actions.ts (performAny, SWITCHED_ACTIONS in src/app/reads.ts), and the read-back sheet is drawn by src/screens/Workspace.tsx. This folder holds its route, its Help article and its AI tools; src/app/reads.ts watchingOn is the one place that asks whether it is on.
A watch is not yet declared as the module's record (AS part 2's records extension point is SW6's), so a build without the module still loads, carries and saves watches as the core's.

get_my_work, get_goal and get_activity are core tools: with Watching off get_my_work leaves out what you watch, but get_goal still names who watches a goal and get_activity still takes watching=1 (spec 6.2; SW3).
